name: One Light

provenance.bg.inset: choice: the syntax palette has no chrome tone
provenance.bg.surface: spec: @syntax-cursor-line = fade(@syntax-fg, 5%) -> derived: mono_1 @5% over bg [blend(mono_1, syntax_bg, 0.05)]
provenance.bg.overlay: choice: = bg.surface (no popup tone in the syntax palette) [derived: blend(mono_1, syntax_bg, 0.05)]
provenance.bg.stripe: derived: bg.base darkened to 1.05:1 (weakest fill; bg.inset is invisible here, 1.00:1 vs inactive selection 1.09:1) - zebra rules in layout-archetypes §2.4
provenance.fg.on-accent: choice: background tone on the saturated accents
provenance.border.default: spec: @syntax-guide = fade(@syntax-fg, 20%) (indent/wrap guides) -> derived over bg [blend(mono_1, syntax_bg, 0.2)]

notes: No official One Light terminal port exists and the Atom source is HSL-only (archived 2018): every hex is derived from atom/one-light-syntax styles/colors.less.

derived: terminal.ansi is NOT official. It is a hue mapping of the syntax palette so the theme loads and 16-color previews work: 0 mono_1, 1 hue-5 red, 2 hue-4 green, 3 hue-6-2 orange, 4 hue-2 blue, 5 hue-3 purple, 6 hue-1 cyan, 7 mono_3, 8 mono_2, 9 hue-5-2 red, 10 hue-4 green, 11 hue-6 orange, 12 syntax_accent, 13 hue-3 purple, 14 hue-1 cyan, 15 selection.

ansi16 overrides (hue-aware nearest slot that clears the contract floor; dim modelled as 55% blend): status.error -> '9' (slot 1 is 3.51:1; slot 9 is the closer match to #ca1243; slot 9 = #ca1243, 5.47:1) | status.warning -> '11' (slot 3 is 3.06:1; slot 11 is the closer match to #986801; slot 11 = #986801, 4.66:1) | search.match -> '11 bold' (slot 11 is the closer match to #986801; slot 11 = #986801, 4.66:1) | diff.changed -> '3' (slot 4 #4078f2 is not the #f2a60d hue; slot 3 = #c18401, 3.06:1) | ramp.mid -> '11' (slot 11 is the closer match to #986801; slot 11 = #986801, 4.66:1) | ramp.high -> '9' (slot 9 is the closer match to #ca1243; slot 9 = #ca1243, 5.47:1) | fg.muted -> '8' (default 'default dim' resolves to 3.05:1; now 5.01:1)
